naslov: NBA breakout players: 30 ready for the next step (yes, even Wemby and Luka)
tekst:
Career progression can take many forms in the NBA: cracking the starting lineup, earning a first All-Star selection or making the leap into the MVP conversation, to name a few.
Let's survey which players are primed for breakout campaigns by first acknowledging that "breakout" can have very different meanings depending on a player's talent and experience.
The 30 players listed below are all primed to take the next step in 2026-27 and have been sorted into tiers based on their current credentials and the circumstances contributing to their projected improvement.
Jump to a tier:
Breakouts to: MVP | Superstar | All-Star | Starter
Breakout picks featuring: Recent trades | Rookies
Tier 1: First MVP?
Who makes the cut: Multitime All-Stars who could conceivably break through to their first MVP in 2026-27.
Victor Wembanyama, Spurs
Last season, Wembanyama finished third in MVP voting and led the Spurs to the Finals during his age-22 campaign, cementing his status as the NBA's top blue-chip prospect since LeBron James. After proving he could captain an elite defense and survive the Western Conference's playoff gauntlet, the French center must refine his isolation scoring game and become a more dependable closer to claim the "Best in the World" throne. Given his rapid improvement during his first three seasons, those developments feel like a matter of "when," not "if."
Luka Doncic, Lakers
The Lakers have fully recalibrated around the 27-year-old Doncic, who is perennially one of the league's top scorers and passers. Doncic has never finished higher than third in MVP voting, but his candidacy should benefit from a new-look supporting cast that's tailored to his strengths and an expected spike in usage after James' offseason departure. Doncic's health looms as a potential drawback: His best chance to win MVP relies on the Lakers finishing with 50-plus wins, a bar they won't clear if he misses significant time.
Cade Cunningham, Pistons
The low-key Cunningham might not generate as much buzz as some of his contemporaries, but he checks all the boxes for aspiring MVPs by putting up big numbers, driving wins and serving as the reliable face of a Finals contender. The 2021 No. 1 pick finished fifth in MVP voting last season after leading Detroit to 60 wins and the East's No. 1 seed. If the Pistons defy their preseason doubters and finish in the conference's top tier again, the 25-year-old Cunningham will almost certainly show up on more ballots this time around.
Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves
Similar to Wembanyama and Cunningham, Edwards is another former No. 1 pick on the ascent. The 25-year-old shooting guard hasn't yet finished in the top five for MVP voting, but he has led the Timberwolves on multiple deep postseason runs and is flanked by a potent new sidekick in LaMelo Ball. Though Edwards' advanced statistics often leave something to be desired compared to past MVP winners, he has a decent chance to win his first scoring title and arguably already leads the league in charisma.
Tyrese Maxey, 76ers
Maxey is a model of continual improvement: His scoring average increased from year to year in each of his first six seasons, and he followed his first All-Star selection in 2024 with his first All-NBA nod in 2026. Philadelphia's lightning-quick guard has mastered his scoring craft, and he's bound to get more national attention playing alongside James and Jaylen Brown on the souped-up 76ers. Though Dwyane Wade, Kyrie Irving and Anthony Davis never generated much traction as MVP candidates while playing in James' shadow, the star dynamic is different in Philadelphia given that Maxey is 25 and James is 41.
Tier 2: All-Star to superstar?
Who makes the cut: Players with at least one All-Star selection who could vault into the top-15 conversation by season's end.
Scottie Barnes, Raptors
To date, the 25-year-old Barnes hasn't really functioned as a prototypical alpha scorer or proven to be a knockdown perimeter shooter. That's OK because the Raptors' forward is a very good offensive player, an exceptional defender and a strong fit alongside Kawhi Leonard. Though Barnes' winning qualities might have been masked during Toronto's rebuilding years, they should be on full display now that the Raptors expect to make playoff progress with Leonard in the fold. His positional versatility on defense, his comfort playing on and off the ball, and his imposing physicality are rarely found in a player.
 Chet Holmgren, Thunder
Now is a good time to buy low on the 24-year-old Holmgren, whose poor showing against Wembanyama's Spurs in the conference finals prompted plenty of social media criticism. The 2022 No. 2 pick is arguably the league's best rim protector other than Wembanyama, and he's a skilled complementary scorer who can finish inside over smaller defenders and step out beyond the arc to beat traditional big men with his jumper. Oklahoma City's deep bench has given Holmgren the luxury of playing under 30 minutes per game throughout his career, but he's a prime candidate to pick up the offensive slack after Jalen Williams' serious ankle injury.
Jalen Johnson, Hawks
Johnson emerged as a fantasy basketball superstar last season thanks to his eye-popping production. In reality, he still has some work to do. Though the 24-year-old forward received the keys to Atlanta's offense after Trae Young's departure, the Hawks were left scrambling for answers when he faltered during the playoffs. A little patience was in order, as Johnson barely played as a rookie and missed most of the 2024-25 season because of injury. Now, his reputation is set to soar if he can lead a deep and talented Hawks team on a real playoff run.

Who makes the cut: Big names aspiring for their first All-Star selection.
